claims.text: Pulse oximetry for everyone, and a chest x-ray unless it is clearly a mild or moderate flare of a known condition.
claims.quote: Pulse oximetry should be performed in all patients, and chest radiography should be done as well unless symptoms are clearly caused by a mild or moderate exacerbation of a known condition.

claims.text: ECG for most adults to detect ischemia, with cardiac biomarkers if suspicion is high.
claims.quote: Most adults should have an ECG to detect myocardial ischemia (and serum cardiac biomarker testing if suspicion is high) unless myocardial ischemia can be excluded clinically.

claims.text: ABG with severe or worsening respiratory status; a basic metabolic panel's bicarbonate helps judge how chronic a respiratory acidosis is.
claims.quote: In patients with severe or deteriorating respiratory status, arterial blood gases (ABGs) should be measured to more precisely quantify PaO2 and PaCO2, diagnose acid-base disorders stimulating hyperventilation, and calculate the alveolar-arterial oxygen gradient. Also, obtaining a basic metabolic panel to measure the bicarbonate level can be useful to assess the chronicity of a respiratory acidosis.

claims.text: Pulmonary embolism: CT angiography or V/Q scan at moderate or high risk; D-dimer at low risk, where a normal level effectively excludes it.
claims.quote: Patients who have no clear diagnosis after chest radiograph and ECG and are at moderate or high risk of having pulmonary embolism (based on a clinical prediction rule) should undergo CT angiography or ventilation/perfusion scanning. Patients who are at low risk may have D-dimer testing (a normal D-dimer level effectively excludes pulmonary embolism in a low-risk patient).

claims.text: Chronic dyspnea: CT, pulmonary function tests, echocardiography and bronchoscopy; cardiopulmonary exercise testing if the workup is inconclusive.
claims.quote: Chronic dyspnea may warrant additional tests, such as CT, pulmonary function tests, echocardiography, and bronchoscopy. If initial workup is inconclusive, cardiopulmonary exercise testing can be considered.
